1. Vide this exparte judgment, I shall dispose of an application filed by Farida (hereinafter referred as "the aggrieved person'') u/s 12 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (hereinafter referred as "Act"), against her husband i.e respondent no.1 (Sharafat) and her inlaws,
i.e. Sh. Shaukat (fatherinlaw), Smt. Vakila (motherin law), Sadaqat (Dever) and Smt. Sabila (Deverani) (hereinafter referred as ''the respondents'').

1 2.
It is alleged in the application that the aggrieved person married to the respondent no.1 on 17.01.2001 according to Muslim rites and customs at New Delhi.
The parents of the aggrieved gave handsome dowry as well as valuable golden and silver ornaments as per their capacity.

Thereafter,
aggrieved joined her matrimonial house in a joint family and she used to prepare food for all the family members.
It is alleged that after 2 years of marriage a son (namely, Suhail) was born to the aggrieved, who became handicapped due to the continuous beatings given by the respondents.

It is further alleged that out of the said wedlock total four children have been born and the elder three children, namely, Suhail, Iqra, Shoeb, are in the custody of the respondent no.1, while the youngest son Sufaiyan is in the custody of the aggrieved.
It is further alleged that after marriage, the husband and other in laws started beating the aggrieved by raising demand of dowry.
It is further alleged that her inlaws started taunting her for bringing insufficient dowry.

It is further alleged that dever of the aggrieved had evil eyes on the aggrieved and tried to outrage her modesty and her deverani also supported him in the said act by stating that 'Ik din mere pati ke saath so jayegi to kya farak padega'.
It is further alleged that respondents used to fight with the aggrieved over petty issues without any valid reasons.

She further alleged that in order to save her marital life her parents gave approx.
Rs.1,70,000/ to the respondents.

She further alleged that her inlaws used to instigate her husband (respondent no.1) to harass and give divorce to the aggrieved and they also used to demand money from the parents of the aggrieved for purchase of a truck for respondent no.1, and on refusal,
aggrieved
was abused and beaten up.

It is further alleged that respondent no.1 is working as a driver and he did not come home for about 1015 days, due to which her fatherinlaw, motherinlaw,
dever and devrani, got benefit to give beatings to the aggrieved for demand of dowry and they have also not provided food and other necessities of life to the aggrieved.

3. It is further alleged that her motherinlaw Shakila in connivance and collusion with one Ahsan,
on 08/09.11.2013 had sent said Ahsan at the parental home of the aggrieved on pretext of compromise and for bringing her back to the matrimonial house and while the aggrieved was alone in her parental home, said Ahsan committed forced rape upon the aggrieved against her wish and consent.

It is further alleged that when aggrieved visited her matrimonial home and informed her husband regarding the said incident, her husband instead of supporting her, started abusing her and also said that the aggrieved is having love affair with him and had made physical relations of her own consent and gave severe beatings to her and also threw her out of the house.
She further alleged that she later came to know that she was raped by Ahsan under a preplanned conspiracy by her husband and other in laws in order to get rid of her.
4. It is further alleged that the aggrieved had borne all the cruelties caused by the respondents with the hope that one day good sense will prevail upon them.

It is further alleged that the father of the aggrieved had borne all the expenses of the aggrieved and had also fulfilled illegal demands of the respondents and had paid Rs.50,000/ in total three times to her inlaws, but the behaviour of the husband and the inlaws of the aggrieved remained abusive.

It is further alleged that on 13.02.2014,
the aggrieved was turned out from her matrimonial home by her inlaws after severe beatings given to her for not fulfilling the demand of dowry.

It is further alleged that on 25.02.2014, motherin law of the aggrieved came to her parents house and the matter was compromised in the presence of respectable persons of the society, but the aggrieved was not taken back to her matrimonial home.
It is further alleged that the husband of the aggrieved and inlaws made a demand of Rs. 1 lakh for Court In Gaurav Sondhi vs . Divya Sondhi - 120 Dlt (2005) 426.

2 bringing her back to the matrimonial home, but her parents being poor persons, are unable to fulfil the illegal demands of the respondents.
5.
It is further alleged that respondent used to behave with the aggrieved like a 'Aaya/maid' and she was made to do all the household work.
It is further alleged that due to constant and repeated cruelties, harassment and beatings, aggrieved suffered a mental shock and depression and she is not able to talk/speak properly.
It is further alleged that entire dowry/istridhan articles belonging to the aggrieved including jewellery, have been kept with the respondents in her matrimonial house.

It is further alleged that aggrieved as well as her family members made various efforts to resolve the matter and requested the respondents to bring back the aggrieved to her matrimonial home,
however, the respondents were bent upon their demands of money.

6. It is further alleged that respondent no.1 has willfully neglected and refused to maintain the aggrieved, even though he is working as a driver of heavy vehicles by profession and earning Rs.25,000/per month from two shops, and is also having certain other movable and immovable properties in his name.
It is further alleged that on 18.03.2014, aggrieved came to know that respondent no.1 had remarried with another lady.
The aggrieved made a complaint before CAW Cell on 16.05.2014.
Being aggrieved with the atrocities of the respondents, the aggrieved Farida had filed the present case to pray for various reliefs under PWDV Act.
7. Domestic incident report was summoned in this case which was filed by the Protection Officer.
8. From the record it appears that notice of the present petition was only issued to respondent no. 1 and notice to respondent no. 2 to 5 was declined.
9. The respondent no.1 had not appeared before the court despite service and he was proceeded ex parte on 26.09.2014.

10. The aggrieved had tendered her exparte evidence by way of affidavit alongwith certain additional documents which are as follows :
I. Evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.CW1/1.
II.
Copy of complaint dated 16.05.2014 is Ex.CW1/A. III.

A copy of marriage card is Ex. CW1/B.
11.
I have heard exparte final arguments and have perused the record.

12. In order to claim any relief under the Domestic Violence Act, it is imperative for the aggrieved person to show that she shared domestic relationship with the respondent and she was subjected to domestic violence during the said period.
Domestic Relationship Court In Gaurav Sondhi vs . Divya Sondhi - 120 Dlt (2005) 426.

3 13.

The term Domestic Relationship is defined in Section 2(f) which reads as under:
''Domestic relationship'' means a relationship between two persons who live or have,
at any point of time, lived together in a shared household, when they are related by consanguinity, marriage, or through a relationship in the nature of marriage,
adoption or are family members living together as a joint family.:

14. It is primafacie evident from the marriage card Ex.CW1/B and the averments made in the petition that the aggrieved person is a legally wedded wife of the respondent no. 1 and after their marriage they had stayed together alongwith all other respondents in their matrimonial home.
The factum of domestic relationship between aggrieved and the respondent no.1, thus, stands established.
Domestic Violence 15.

The term Domestic Violence is defined in Section 3 which reads as under:
"Any Act, omission or commission or conduct of the respondent shall constitute domestic violence in case it  (a) harms or injuries or endangers the health, safety, life, limb or wellbeing, whether mental or physical, of the aggrieved person or tends to do so and includes causing physical abuse, sexual abuse, verbal and emotional abuse and economic abuse; or (b) harasses, harms, injures or endangers the aggrieved person with a view to coerce her or any other person related to her to meet any unlawful demand for any dowry or other property or valuable security; or (c) has the effect of threatening the aggrieved person or any person related to her by any conduct mentioned in clause (a) or clause (b); or (d) otherwise injures or causes harms, whether physical or mental, to the aggrieved person."
16. As the respondent no.1 has been proceeded exparte, thus, for the purpose of disposing of the present matter, the evidence led by the aggrieved is being completely relied upon.

17. In order to prove her case, the aggrieved person had relied upon the averments made by her in her application U/s 12 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 and her evidence by way of affidavit.

Accordingly, the aggrieved person has been able to prove on the balance of probabilities that respondent no.1 has committed certain acts of verbal and emotional abuses upon her.
Certain acts of physical abuse and economic abuse also appear to have been committed upon the aggrieved by the respondent no.1 in view of the complaint filed by the aggrieved before CAW Cell.

As the aggrieved person has been able to establish a prima facie case of domestic violence in her favour qua respondent no.1, she is entitled to claim various reliefs under the Domestic Violence Act, 2005.
18. Now, I shall deal with the relief sought by the aggrieved person.

Reliefs:
Protection Order U/s 18 of the Act :
19.
Aggrieved has not prayed for any specific protection order.
Further, it is an admitted fact that the aggrieved and the respondent no.1 are residing separately.
Therefore, there is no need for passing any protection order.
The said relief is declined.

Residence Order U/s 19 of the Act:
20.
The aggrieved has not prayed for any specific residential order, therefore, the said relief is being denied.

Maintenance Order U/s 20 of the Act :
21.
The aggrieved has prayed for a sum of Rs. 5,000/per month as maintenance.

The law on granting interim maintenance is clear that the aggrieved as well as her children, if any are entitled to get monetary relief which should be adequate, fair and reasonable and consistent with the standard of living to which the aggrieved person is accustomed.
In the present case, there were four children born to the parties, out of which only one of the minor child, namely, Sufiyan, is in the custody of the aggrieved.
Aggrieved has not shown any source of her income.
She alleged that the respondent no.1 is a driver of heavy vehicles and earns some rentals from his shops and other assets, and thereby she alleged his income to be at least Rs.25,000/ per month.
However, no documentary or other evidence was led by the aggrieved to prove the said income.
No details of any assets in the name of respondent no.1 was also proved by the aggrieved.
22. Hence, as the respondent is a able bodied man and since no educational qualification of respondent no.1 has been stated, he is assumed to be an unskilled labourer.

Since the aggrieved is the legally wedded wife of the respondent, and she herself has no other means to sustain herself,
thus, it is a legal duty of the respondent no.1 to maintain her.
Accordingly, as per the Minimum Wages Act, I assume that respondent would be at least earning minimum wages of an unskilled labourer i.e Rs.8,000/ per month.
Therefore, on the scale of balance of convenience, I deem it fit to award a sum of Rs.4,000/ per month to the aggrieved as interim maintenance for herself and her minor child.
The amount shall be payable from the date of filing of the petition till further orders.
